description:
FOUND s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the DOCUMENTATION parse-acceptance run: it is the FIRST code example of perlfaq4 (`print int(0.6/0.2-2), "\n";`).  ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/probes/floatminus.pl + divminus.pl:

    print 0.5-1, "\n";        perl -0.5     PCL: statement dropped ... Missing case: ['Token::Number::Float<0.5>','Token::Number<-1>']
    print $x*0.5-1;  print 2.5-0.5;         dropped too
    $x/2-1   3-1   1e3-1   0x10-1            all fine (an INTEGER / exp / hex literal before `-1` is lexed right)
    PPI dump of `print 0.5-1;`:  Word<print> Number::Float<0.5> Number<-1> Structure<;>      expected: Float<0.5> Operator<-> Number<1>

Sibling of docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md §15 (`)` followed by `-1`: the operator is swallowed into a negative number) -- the same repair family (`_repair_*` in the `_ppi_parse` token passes: a Number whose content starts with `-`/`+` and whose previous significant token ENDS A TERM is split into Operator + Number); check that §15's repair keys on "previous token ends a term" and simply lacks Number::Float in its term-ender set (then the fix is one class name), and probe the other literal classes while there: `1.5e3-1`, `.5-1`, `1_000.5-1`, `0.5+1`, version strings `v1.2-1`.  Every fragment re-parse goes through Pl::Parser::fragment_doc (#435).
Rule 13 in the SAME commit: ppi-upstream-bugs.md section, docs/ppi-bug-report.t row (bump tests =>), canary in Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t.

=== DONE (s543d) (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21) ===
VERDICT: FIXED on main since s527a -- this is docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md §34 (`0.5-1 => Float<0.5> Number<-1>` is one of its dump rows), fixed on PCL's PPI branch by group A (`a737c524`: `_opcontext` reads a number of any kind as the end of a term).  PCL's PPI lexes `print 0.5-1;` as `Number::Float<0.5> Operator<-> Number<1>`.
PROBES (scratch/s543d/p1, 51 rows, perl 5.40.3 vs main 64353611 vs the s543d tree): every spelling of a number before `-N` (`0.5-1`, `$x*0.5-1`, `int(0.6/0.2-2)`, `.5-1`, `1_000.5-1`, `1e3-1`, `1.5E-3-1`, `0x1f-1`, `0b11-1`, `07-1`, `1.-1`, `v1.2-1`, `1.2.3-1`), a `)` `]` `}`, a variable, a quote, a postfix `++`, a list slice (#2541), `1..-1`, and the negative-literal controls (`print -1`, `return -1`, `(1, -1)`, `2*-1`, `2**-1`, `x => -1`, `-1` at a statement start, `-3**2`, `-1.5**2`, `K -1` after `use constant`): 51 of 51 = perl on main AND on the tree.
THE TERM END PPI STILL MISSED: `__LINE__-1` (and `__FILE__.1`, `__LINE__.5`, `__LINE__ %h`) -- the expect-state checker's three `minus-in-number` rows on the populations were all `__LINE__-1` (perl's t/op/coreamp.t 1141, Test-Simple t/Legacy/plan.t 17 and use_ok.t 87).  Catalogued as §68 and fixed on the branch: group BB (`b341df79`, the five FUN0OP words join `%NO_OPERAND`).  `__FILE__.1` was a statement DROP on main (p1b: main 16 of 19 = perl, tree 19 of 19).  Guard: Pl/t/ppi-token-rows-01.t (§68 row, inverse-verified on main), registry row §68, the twins.
`Pl::PExpr::_fix_ppi_negative_number_bug` KEPT: its `-N**2` arm reads PPI's negative literal (a precedence rule, not a PPI bug) and its bareword arm is the prototype table's (`K -1`); s543d's audit counts them (docs/ppi-fix-at-source-s527.md §10).
subject: NEW PPI 1.291 MIS-LEX (rule 13 owed), LOUD and everyday: a FLOAT literal followed by `-DIGIT` lexes as two NUMBERS -- `0.5-1`, `$x*0.5-1`, `int(0.6/0.2-2)` => whole statement DROPPED, the program dies "statement not supported"
triage_reason: PPI mis-lex: a float literal followed by `-DIGIT` (LOUD, everyday; the PPI branch)
